provenance.notes: Clean family batch, book archetype. Tiny tickets that only work as twice-a-year routes, so products stay very cheap and route-shaped. Kept to recurring cleaning; guard installation belongs to the ext family's gutters kit. Fresh Fern fails CTA contrast. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.section: What a gutter cleaning visit includes
pageStructurePlus.contains: Hand-cleaning every trough, flushing each downspout, bagging and hauling debris, clearing roof valleys above the gutters, and a check for loose hangers and leaking seams
pageStructurePlus.why: Cheap crews blow debris onto the lawn and leave. A written visit list is how a careful gutter cleaner justifies the price.

pageStructurePlus.contains: When oaks, maples, pines and seed-dropping trees shed in this area, when to book the autumn gutter clean, and when a second late visit makes sense
pageStructurePlus.why: Homeowners book too early and pay twice. Timing the visit to their trees shows expertise and fills the route in the right weeks.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Clogged downspout elbows, underground drain lines, pop-up emitters, splash blocks, and what to do when water pools at the foundation
pageStructurePlus.why: Overflow often starts at a blocked downspout, not the gutter. Explaining it wins the jobs a basic cleaning would miss.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Photos from the roofline before and after cleaning, each downspout flow-tested on video, and notes on damage spotted, sent the same day
pageStructurePlus.why: Nobody can see inside their gutters from the ground. Photos are the only proof the job was done, and they turn one visit into a yearly customer.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Ladder standoffs that keep weight off the gutter, two- and three-story homes, steep pitches, tile and slate roofs, and when a job needs a second person
pageStructurePlus.why: Owners of tall or delicate roofs worry about damage more than price. Showing how each roof is approached wins those houses.

openers.line: Your Google listing has good gutter cleaning reviews and no Website button, so someone watching water spill over the gutter in the rain can't see a price or book a date.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Where that overflowing gutter search could land: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website link on your listing opens Facebook, where the gutter cleaning price for a two-story house is buried in the comments under a leaf photo.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link. Note where it lands and whether any price is visible.
openers.linkLine: Your gutter cleaning prices on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: The site on your listing is a free page with last autumn's gutter special and a form that doesn't send. In leaf season, that form is a full route you never saw.
openers.hook: Open the site and find one broken thing: a dead form, an old special, an old number. Note it.
openers.linkLine: A gutter cleaning page with booking that works: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your gutter page wouldn't scroll on my phone. People book this standing in the yard, looking up at a gutter with a plant growing out of it.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Gutter cleaning, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Nothing online says what gutter cleaning costs for a ranch versus a two-story, so the homeowner books whoever shows a number, even a crew that leaves the debris on the lawn.
openers.hook: Check the listing, posts and any site for a published price. If there is none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Gutter cleaning prices by house size: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your before-and-after shots of packed gutters from the roofline are proof homeowners can't get from the ground, and they disappear down the feed in days.
openers.hook: Find one before-and-after gutter post and note the house type. Name it if they reply.
openers.linkLine: A gutter before-and-after gallery that stays: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews say the overflow over the front door finally stopped after your visit. That's exactly what the next person searching for gutter cleaning wants to read.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about overflow, downspouts or tidiness. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your gutter reviews beside the Book button: {demo-link}

openers.line: Whole streets want their gutters cleaned in the same few weeks after the leaves drop. The gutter cleaner whose route dates are bookable online fills those weeks first.
openers.hook: Use from late September to November. Check for a post about autumn booking.
openers.linkLine: Autumn gutter cleaning route dates, bookable: {demo-link}

openers.line: Spring seed pods and pine needles clog gutters right when the heavy rains come. A spring gutter cleaning page catches people before the first overflow.
openers.hook: Use from March to May. Look for any spring cleaning posts.
openers.linkLine: Spring gutter cleaning, booked before the rain: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring help for the gutter cleaning season. Good applicants check whether the outfit looks steady before they climb ladders for you.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A gutter cleaning page with a hiring section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your gutter reviews come from {Neighborhood} and the tree-lined streets near it, but nothing online shows your route areas, so the next neighbourhood over never asks.
openers.hook: Find the neighbourhoods named in their reviews and use the leafiest one.
openers.linkLine: A route map for your gutter cleaning areas: {demo-link}

openers.line: If customers already have you back every spring and fall, a gutter cleaning plan they sign up for once fills the route without a single reminder call.
openers.hook: Look for reviews that say 'every year' or 'twice a year'. Quote one.
openers.linkLine: A twice-a-year gutter cleaning plan sign-up: {demo-link}

openers.line: Someone on a ladder at the second story is a worry for any homeowner. If your gutter crew is insured, that belongs on the page beside the price.
openers.hook: Look for 'insured' on their listing, truck or posts. Never claim what you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Insurance and roof-safe access on one gutter page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like your gutter jobs spread street by street when one neighbour sees your ladder out. Those neighbours look you up next and find only a number.
openers.hook: Search local Facebook groups or Nextdoor for their name. Quote a recommendation if you find one.
openers.linkLine: Where a neighbour who saw your ladder should land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is the gutter problem homeowners dread finding. It belongs on a page where they can book the same clean-out.
openers.hook: Pick their newest gutter post and name it: the seedlings, the packed downspout, the three-story house.
openers.linkLine: That gutter job on a page that books: {demo-link}

objections.objection: Gutter cleaning is too cheap to need a website.
objections.handler: "One gutter clean is cheap. A customer who signs up for spring and fall for years isn't. The site sells the plan, and the plan is what makes the route pay."

objections.objection: I'm slammed in the fall and dead in summer.
objections.handler: "That's the point of the plan page. Customers sign up in summer for their autumn date, so your fall route is full before the leaves drop."

objections.objection: My customers just call me every year.
objections.handler: "Good. The site lets them sign up once and stop calling, and it gives their neighbours somewhere to book when they see your ladder."

objections.objection: I don't want to post prices, houses vary.
objections.handler: "Show a starting price by single-story and two-story, and say steep roofs or big debris loads are confirmed on site. People who only wanted a number stop calling."

objections.objection: I already get jobs from an app.
objections.handler: "Those jobs get sent to several gutter cleaners and you pay either way. A neighbour who finds your own site only gets you."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's house-size pricing, the plan sign-up, the leaf timing page and photo reports. A handful of twice-a-year gutter customers covers it."

sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} gutter demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — the leaves are coming down in {City}, and after the first gutter overflow people search for a cleaner that night. Thought of you.

The site is still here whenever you want it, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a year of a handful of twice-a-year plan customers, never to one gutter clean.
The house-size price list and the plan sign-up are the core. Everything else is small and optional.
Keep every add-on cheap; this trade's tickets are small and owners compare everything to one job.
Price the photo report feature by how it's delivered: a texted link per job costs more to set up than a gallery.
Sell in summer for the autumn route, and in late winter for the spring route.
Leave guard installation to the gutters kit; here, mention guards only as a referral or a later conversation.

withoutAI.route: Gutter guard installers they refer to
withoutAI.whoPays: The guard installer, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The guard installer you point gutter customers toward still quotes from a pickup truck notebook. I'd build their estimate site on your introduction."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Cleaners and guard installers pass customers both ways, and the introduction comes with a warm word.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The roofer you call when you spot lifted shingles from the gutter line has a gallery from years ago. Introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Roofers have bigger tickets and value the cleaner who spots roof problems for them.

withoutAI.route: Window cleaners on the same houses
withoutAI.whoPays: The window cleaning company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The window cleaner who works your gutter customers' houses books by phone too. Same route-and-plan layout."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Both sell seasonal exterior visits to the same homeowners and already swap referrals.

withoutAI.route: Tree trimmers over the same roofs
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The tree crew you recommend when branches overhang a gutter has no estimate form online. Your word gets me in."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Tree work is a larger ticket, and the gutter cleaner sees the overhanging branches first.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The HOA manager who books your street-wide gutter days sends notices on paper. A resident site with service dates is a quick build."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: HOA managers trust the vendor residents already like, and they pay to cut notice work.

withoutAI.route: Pressure washers who do the same exteriors
withoutAI.whoPays: The pressure washing company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The soft-wash crew that cleans the gutter faces after you clear the inside needs a booking site with a house-size price too."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Gutter cleaning and exterior washing are sold to the same homes, often the same week.

withAI.route: Photo quote for the guard installer
withAI.pitchLine: "Gutter cleaning customers send a photo of the house and the run length, and the guard installer gets a draft quote to approve."
withAI.whyItWorks: Built for a business the cleaner already refers to, so the introduction carries weight.

withAI.pitchLine: "Photos from the gutter line get scanned for lifted shingles or flashing gaps, and the roofer gets a list of houses worth a call."
withAI.whyItWorks: Roofers want warm leads, and the gutter cleaner is already on the roof edge twice a year.

withAI.pitchLine: "Window and gutter visits for the same house get offered on the same day, with the schedule drafted for both crews."

withAI.route: Overhang check for the tree service
withAI.pitchLine: "The gutter crew's roof photos get flagged for branches touching the roof, and the tree service gets a draft trimming quote list."
withAI.whyItWorks: Tree services need a steady stream of small jobs, and the gutter route finds them.

withAI.route: Service day notices for HOA managers
withAI.pitchLine: "Residents get service day notices and answers about which gutter and exterior vendors come when, drafted from the HOA's own calendar."

withAI.route: House-size quote helper for pressure washers
withAI.pitchLine: "Customers enter their address and house size, and the soft-wash crew gets a draft quote, the same tool built for gutter pricing."
withAI.whyItWorks: Already working for a business the pressure washer knows, so the pitch is short.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back with gutter prices
softwareAI.pitchLine: "You're on a ladder and miss a call. The caller gets a text with gutter cleaning prices by house size and a booking link within a minute."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs the business number forwarded and wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Route-day reminder text
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Plan customers get a text two days before their street's gutter day, with a note to move cars from under the downspouts."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the plan list and route dates.

softwareAI.name: Photo report sender

softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs one phone per crew and their photo routine.

softwareAI.name: Route builder by street and tree type
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Gutter plan customers grouped by street and leaf timing, so oak streets get their autumn visit later than maple streets."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs addresses and a rough tree note per street.

softwareAI.name: Booking chat for gutter questions
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'do you do three-story houses' and 'do you haul the debris' from your own gutter answers, then books a route date."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs services, prices and route dates. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for gutter jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When someone writes that the overflow above the porch finally stopped, a short thanks naming that gutter fix is drafted for your thumbs-up."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, alongside review requests. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Plan renewal and card update
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Before each season, gutter plan customers get a renewal note and a link to update their card, so nobody falls off the route by accident."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the plan list and billing setup.

softwareAI.name: Damage notes log by house
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Loose hangers, leaking seams and sagging runs noted with photos per house, so next season's gutter visit starts with what to check."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the photo report and a simple damage checklist.

softwareAI.name: Photo damage summary for homeowners
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The crew's gutter photos get a plain-language note on anything that looks loose or leaking, checked by the owner before it goes to the customer."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, after the photo report. Needs past photos with the owner's notes. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Street group booking page
softwareAI.pitchLine: "One neighbour starts a street day, others join from a link, and the gutter route gets a full street at a group price."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs group pricing rules and route dates.

softwareAI.name: After-hours receptionist for overflow calls
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Someone calls during a storm with gutters pouring over, and the receptionist takes the house size and books the first open gutter slot."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the calendar and prices. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Ladder hand applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants for seasonal gutter crews answer questions about heights, driving and weekends, and you only call the ones who fit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: August or February, before each season. Needs must-haves and pay. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Job costing per route day
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See what each gutter route day earned after drive time, dump fees and labour, so house-size prices are set from real numbers."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, after a full season. Needs route days, hours and costs.

softwareAI.name: Customer message sorter for gutter jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Date changes, 'can you also check the downspout' requests and plan questions get sorted and drafted between gutter jobs."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the business text line or inbox. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Seasonal waitlist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Late sign-ups for a packed leaf-season gutter route queue up by street, so a dropped house is offered straight to its neighbour."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, before the rush. Needs route dates and capacity.

softwareAI.name: Leaf timing note writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each autumn, a short note to plan customers on when their street's trees are dropping and when the gutter crew will come, drafted for the owner."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, before leaf fall. Needs the route builder data. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Guard referral handoff
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a gutter customer ticks 'interested in guards', their photos and house size go to the installer the owner trusts, with a referral note."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the installer's contact and the owner's referral terms.

softwareAI.name: Plan customer page
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Plan customers see their next gutter date, past photo reports and billing, and can add downspout flushing without calling."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the plan list and photo reports.

softwareAI.name: Crew handbook assistant for roof access

softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs written procedures and the owner's approval of every answer. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their disposal routine.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the gutter route builder and plan page
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Gutter cleaning companies, monthly per account
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a twice-a-year route and plan tool for one gutter cleaner. Every small gutter outfit runs its route from a notebook."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first client paid for the route logic, and every seasonal gutter business has the same spring and fall crunch.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: License the plan sign-up to a gutter supply distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Give every gutter contractor on your books a cleaning plan sign-up page, so their customers stay theirs and they keep buying from you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors want contractors with steady work, and a plan tool creates it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer members a gutter cleaning template with house-size pricing, leaf timing and a plan sign-up as a membership perk."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Owner groups need reasons to join, and one agreement reaches many small operators.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Territories selling gutter, window and wash visits need one route sign-up per area. I build the gutter piece once and clone it."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract, many territories, one template from a real operator.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label gutter cleaning template for agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency keeps building small sites for gutter cleaners. License mine with the plan sign-up and photo report done."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell the client; you sell them the part you've already got right.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: HOA management firms' exterior maintenance calendar
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every community you manage gets gutter, window and wash days on one calendar, with vetted vendors and resident notices."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Management firms juggle vendor days across many communities and pay for one view.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Home warranty and maintenance membership companies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Members get spring and fall gutter cleaning booked with vetted local crews, with photo reports on their account."
